questions.q: What do you see with two crossed polarizing filters and no stone?
questions.why: No light gets through any more.

questions.q: An isotropic stone between crossed filters…
choices: lights up four times per turn
questions.why: Garnets, spinel and glass are isotropic.

questions.q: An anisotropic stone turned a full turn lights up…
An aggregate of small crystals (jade, chalcedony) stays…
questions.why: Summary: dark = isotropic, four flashes = anisotropic, bright = aggregate.

questions.q: Which figure does a uniaxial stone show in the conoscope?
choices: A black cross surrounded by coloured rings
questions.why: The cross does not move when the stone is turned.

questions.q: Which stone has a “bull's eye” at the centre of its uniaxial figure?
questions.why: Quartz rotates the plane of polarization along its axis.

choices: A polariscope fitted with a lens, which shows the interference figure
questions.why: The stone is looked at under converging light.

questions.q: What does the figure of a biaxial stone show?
choices: Two “eyes” crossed by dark bands, and the cross that opens into a moustache
questions.why: When the stone is turned, the cross opens into two curved branches.

questions.q: What can a strongly strained isotropic stone show?
choices: Patches or a cross: this is anomalous double refraction
